Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
920 PM EDT Thu Jul 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes to the forecast. A few sprinkles or a brief shower
could skirt Northeast MD over the next hour or two. Afterwards,
dry for a longer period of time.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Increasing shower and thunderstorm chances Sunday through
  early next week as low pressure and a series of fronts cross
  the region.

- 2) Primarily dry conditions through Saturday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Increasing shower and thunderstorm chances
Sunday through early next week as low pressure and a series of 
fronts cross the region.

Back toward the typical summertime regime Sunday into the first half 
of next week with daily chances for showers and thunderstorms. The 
greatest coverage of showers and thunderstorms appears to be Sunday 
into Monday as a potent upper level trough ejects eastward from the 
Great Lakes into the Ohio River Valley. The incumbent upper level 
trough looks to be pinched off as it dives south and east yielding a 
cut low pressure system which looks to cross the area late Sunday 
into Monday. The cutoff low and associated cold front will bring 
widespread shower and thunderstorm chances to the region both days 
along with abundant cloud cover. Shear and instability values look 
to remain low due to weak winds aloft and widespread cloudiness. 
Even with that said, GoogleWxNext2 and NSSL probabilities have 10 to 
30 percent contours over the region during the Sunday and Monday 
timeframe. This will be dictated by the placement and timing of the 
low/associated front as it crosses the region. Moisture will be 
ample ahead of the boundary on southerly flow although instability 
will be lacking with modeled CAPE values less than a few hundred 
j/kg given the extra cloud cover and timing of the system beyond the 
peak heating window. 

Beneficial rainfall is likely given the coverage of showers and 
thunderstorms. Overall looking at half an inch to one inch of rain 
Sunday through the middle of next week. Locally higher totals are 
possible under heavier thunderstorms and across portions of the 
Alleghenies/Shenandoah Valley where the low looks to track through. 
The flooding threat remains lo, but not zero given repetitive rounds 
of thunderstorms (especially over urban/poor drainage areas). 

Beyond Monday, diurnal chances for showers and thunderstorms look to 
continue as the front stalls near or just south of the area. The 
next cold front and upper level trough will follow with another 
round of widespread thunderstorm chances later in the workweek. High 
temperatures will remain at or just above normal through the period. 
Sunday and Monday look to be the coolest with highs in the upper 70s 
and mid 80s. Highs get back close to 90 Tuesday through Thursday 
next week. Overnight lows will fall back into the mid to upper
60s. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Primarily dry conditions through Saturday.

As an upper level low continues to spin over southern New 
England, a few sprinkles or a brief shower could skirt parts of
Northeast MD through the remainder of the evening. Temperatures
will remain seasonable or slightly below normal overnight, when
lighter winds may allow rural areas to decouple. Lows tonight 
from the mid 50s to mid 60s (perhaps locally even cooler in the 
higher elevations).

The surface high will reach the area Friday. Shortwave ridging
will approach from the west as the upper low departs New England.
Dry conditions are expected with high temperatures closer to 
climatology in the mid 80s to near 90 and lows in the 60s to 
around 70.

Temperatures may warm a couple more degrees Saturday as the high
moves off the coast and increasing southerly flow develops.
Clouds will likely start increasing as low pressure at the
surface and aloft moves into the Ohio Valley. There is some
uncertainty with how quickly rain chances arrive. Some showers
could reach the Alleghenies as early as Saturday afternoon, but
recent trends are suggesting it will be delayed until Saturday 
night. Much of the area, especially east of the Blue Ridge, may 
remain dry until Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
VFR conditions. Light winds through Friday as high pressure 
moves overhead.

Southerly flow may become gusty Saturday afternoon. Showers
along with sub-VFR ceilings may reach CHO and MRB late Saturday
night, but confidence is low.

More widespread sub-VFR conditions are expected Sunday as showers 
and thunderstorms return to the terminals due to a front crossing 
the region. The severe weather threat appears low, but not zero at 
this time. Expect temporary restrictions at times due to 
thunderstorms. Gusts will remain out of the south/southeast at less 
than 20 kts. 

Expect sub-VFR conditions to continue at times Monday as the front 
and low pressure system slowly exit the region. The front will stall 
nearby or just to the south of the region Tuesday and Wednesday 
keeping temporary restrictions in place, especially at terminals 
south of the corridor. Winds will blow out of the northeast Monday 
before becoming light and variable midweek.

&&

.MARINE...
Light winds through Friday as high pressure moves overhead. On 
Saturday, wind shifts to southerly with advisories likely by 
afternoon. 

SCA conditions are likely to continue Sunday with showers and 
thunderstorms leading to potential SMWs Sunday afternoon and 
evening. Sub-SCA level winds return Monday through Wednesday next 
week.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies remain steady through the end of the week with 
sensitive tidal locations remaining in Action stage during the 
high tide cycles. This weekend, tidal anomalies rise with 
southerly winds. Annapolis is forecast to approach Minor flood 
stage as early as Saturday morning.
